description: OpenFlights publishes free tables of airports, airlines, routes and aircraft types behind its flight-mapping website. The airports table lists more than 10,000 airports, train stations and ferry terminals with IATA and ICAO codes, coordinates, altitude and time zone (as of January 2017); the airlines table holds 5,888 airlines (as of January 2012); and the route database, compiled with Airline Route Mapper, contains 67,663 routes between 3,321 airports on 548 airlines (as of June 2014), each with airline, source and destination airport, codeshare flag, stops and equipment. The site is run by OpenFlights and its code is on GitHub under AGPL-3.0. Coverage is global at the level of individual airports and airport pairs. Files are plain comma-separated .dat downloads from the GitHub repository; the data is licensed under the Open Database License with contents under the Database Contents License, free with attribution and share-alike, and commercial licences are sold on request. Caveats: the site says the GitHub copy is a sporadically updated snapshot, the route table has not been refreshed since 2014, and daylight-saving rules approximate 2009. The route table is widely used as a ready-made global air network for network flow, cascading failure and resilience studies of airline networks, with airport locations matched to OurAirports, catalogued here.
